summary: A further revised set of ARPANET mailing lists for distributing network documents. List A is the Network Liaison Group, who receive RFCs and other formal documents first, and lists B and C are for other participants and station agents.

eli5.summary: An updated address book for who gets copies of network documents by mail.

subtitle: Three October 1972 distribution lists the Network Information Center used to mail RFCs and other network documents.

tldr.problem: Network documents had to reach the right people at every site quickly, and sites needed to know whom to mail.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC prints three lists with names, postal addresses and phone numbers: A for Network Liaisons, B for NIC distribution to non-site participants, and C for Station Agents.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 363 and shows who received documents in October 1972.

today: RFC 402 obsoletes RFC 363. The names and addresses are those of October 1972 and were never meant to be permanent.

sections.title: Three Distribution Lists
sections.content:
The Network Information Center at Stanford Research Institute issued this on 26 October 1972, obsoleting RFC 363. The abstract says the three lists are for distribution of Network documents.

Each entry gives a site name, a contact person, a postal address and a telephone number.
sections.eli5: The network information office wrote down three mailing lists so documents go to the right people.

sections.title: List A: The Network Liaison Group
sections.content:
List A should be used by sites when they distribute their own documents, to get RFCs to Liaisons as quickly as possible. All but local mail should be sent Air Mail.

The list includes all Network Liaisons and others who should receive initial distribution of RFCs, whether sent from NIC or from sites. They also receive selected catalogs and other formal documents from NIC.
sections.eli5: List A is for the main contact person at each site. They get new documents first, and far-away mail goes by air.

sections.title: Lists B and C
sections.content:
List B names Network participants who are not sites. They receive all formal Network documents sent from NIC, in the mailing to Liaisons when one is made, otherwise when documents go to Station Agents.

List C names the NIC Station Agents. They receive copies of everything sent to Liaisons plus documents sent as part of Station collection. A mailing goes to them once a week, or oftener when quantity warrants.
sections.eli5: List B is for outside friends of the network and list C is for the helpers who keep a document shelf. Helpers get a package every week.

items.title: A: Liaison Group
items.text: Initial distribution of RFCs, from NIC or from sites.

items.title: B: NIC distribution
items.text: Non-site participants who receive formal documents from NIC.

items.title: C: Station Agents
items.text: Copies of all Liaison documents, mailed weekly or oftener.
